content.text:
**I would not sign off on “no tension” yet.** The overall architecture is coherent, but progressive amendments have left conflicting wording and an important dependency gap that could steer another agent incorrectly.

I reviewed all eight listed changes, their shared contracts and task boundaries, and relevant implementation paths. These need reconciliation:

1. **The detail instruction editor is both required and prohibited.**  
   Canonical correction now [requires editing original ingredients and instructions in detail](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/canonical-ingredient-correction/specs/recipe-editing/spec.md:216). Step scaling still says [“SHALL NOT add an inline detail instruction editor”](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/scale-cooking-step-ingredients/specs/recipe-editing/spec.md:7). The editor already exists in source. Remove or explicitly supersede that older prohibition so a later agent cannot interpret it as grounds to remove the editor.

2. **One cooking-report failure scenario contradicts the coherent-refresh rule.**  
   The requirement says to apply report metadata and explicitly refresh changed recipe content. Its launch-failure scenario still says [“cooking applies that recipe”](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/scale-cooking-step-ingredients/specs/cooking/spec.md:102), which could replace active cooking content unexpectedly. [Current code preserves the content snapshot](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/pwa/src/components/planner/CooksMode.tsx:772). The scenario should explicitly require that same behavior on failure.

3. **Unready recipe review needs an explicit Search boundary.**  
   Canonical correction says [review-filtered Search includes flagged unready recipes](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/canonical-ingredient-correction/design.md:98), while the unchanged [typed-search contract requires ready recipes](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/specs/recipe-search/spec.md:498). Source currently permits unready recipes through filter-only review, but [PostgreSQL lexical retrieval still excludes them](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/api/src/RecipeApi/Services/RecipeLexicalSearchRepository.cs:49). Clarify whether typing within that review queue should find them. This is an unresolved boundary, not proof that the whole review queue fails.

4. **Step scaling lacks a complete production-input dependency.**  
   The foundation explicitly records that [ordinary binding production is missing and scaling fixtures seed bindings](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/canonical-ingredient-correction/tasks.md:53). The step tasks principally cover validating and consuming those bindings. Add an explicit producer/semantic-validation task and an ordinary import-to-cooking acceptance journey. Otherwise, projection tests could pass while normal recipes never acquire usable bindings. This is a delivery gap, rather than contradictory arithmetic.

5. **A superseded proposal still appears active.**  
   [Selective ingredient repair explicitly says not to apply it](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/openspec/changes/selective-ingredient-repair/proposal.md:1), but OpenSpec lists it as in progress with five tasks. Its replacement is clear; its lifecycle presentation is misleading. It should be retired explicitly as superseded and unimplemented, without promoting its requirements.

The central rules **do agree**: one canonical content revision, exact original quantities, step allocations adding no grocery demand, checks compared against their saved baseline, and recovery preserving identities and human corrections. Bilingual identity and grocery interaction ownership are compatible. The recovery prerequisite extraction also explains the apparent dependency cycle. I found no additional semantic conflict in Similar Search or browser-parity work.

**Validation:** strict OpenSpec validation passed **44/44**, with no duplicate capability/requirement targets across active changes. Reviewed OpenSpec inputs stayed unchanged throughout. These checks establish structural consistency—not runtime integration. I changed no repository files and ran no application tests.

I recommend reconciling these specific artifacts before further dependent implementation; the evidence does not call for redesigning the whole change set.

**There is substantial implementation already in place, but several missing connections prevent the changes from being complete.** The unchecked task counts overstate how much needs rebuilding; some large tasks contain implemented behavior alongside unfinished integration and acceptance.

I reviewed the eight active changes, the shared **C01–C53 scenarios**, source/tests, recorded qualification evidence, and current hosted CI.

| Change | Already built | What remains |
|---|---|---|
| **canonical-ingredient-correction** | Canonical content/revisions, stable ingredient IDs, exact quantities, guarded ingredient/step editing, draft recovery, staged publication, flagged correction, fresh URL import and its narrow reviewed recovery. | Finish other import channels and general guarded reimport. Photo work is currently uncommitted; PDF, synthesis and shared-recipe imports are not fully canonical. Complete ordinary production of structured package/unit facts and reconcile legacy-edit compatibility. |
| **scale-cooking-step-ingredients** | Projection engine for whole, absolute, fractional, remainder, fixed and per-item uses; stale-binding protection; coherent refresh; prepared-count behavior; Cook UI cleanup. | **Create trusted bindings through ordinary application workflows.** Existing scaling fixtures supply bindings themselves. Complete producer-to-Cook acceptance and final qualification. |
| **bilingual-shopping-identity** | Reserved identity fields and recovery validation structures; existing conservative name/unit handling. | Most of the feature: adopt the vocabulary, persist validated mappings, group by saved food identity, select EN/FR labels, protect mapping/category corrections, and qualify recovery. |
| **migrate-canonical-recipe-model** | Guarded per-recipe conversion, canonical backup/seed/sync support, integrity checks, and existing exact-recovery machinery. | Operational conversion entry point, dry-run/resume manifests, deferred-recipe handling, full current-format recovery/cutover qualification, first-list safeguards, old-client rehearsal and rollback packet. |
| **restore-dependable-grocery-interactions** | Stable row checks, concurrency protection, exact checked-demand baselines, range/incomplete-demand handling, focus/category behavior and removal of obsolete warnings. | Primarily final qualification on the release candidate. Bilingual grouping remains owned by its separate change. |
| **restore-local-ci-browser-parity** | Shared production-browser runner, impact selection, CI wiring and several repaired fixtures. | Resolve the current hosted failure and demonstrate the required local/hosted results on the same candidate. |
| **similar-search-filter** | Existing Similar search/removal behavior. | The proposed compact control row, count semantics, accessible overflow, localized labels, and navigation-versus-typing focus behavior. This remains a distinct UI implementation. |
| **selective-ingredient-repair** | Explicitly superseded. | **Nothing should be implemented from this change.** Its active lifecycle status needs reconciliation. |

The most consequential gaps are these:

1. **Step scaling has a consumer but no ordinary producer.**  
   The [projection engine explicitly never discovers ingredient uses](/Users/alex/Code/whats-for-supper/api/src/RecipeApi/Services/CookingStepProjection.cs:8).
